hero.h1: Trenchless Sewer Repair in Elgin, IL
hero.sub: Replacing a sewer line used to mean a trench from the house to the street. Today most Elgin lines can be lined or replaced through small openings. We camera the line first, then give you a flat price for the method that fits. From our office on North McLean Boulevard.

img.alt: Two J. Blanton plumbers pouring resin into a sewer liner bag to prepare a trenchless pipe lining

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: Trenchless sewer repair, also called no-dig sewer repair, fixes a damaged pipe without digging a trench along its full length. Instead of opening up your yard from the house to the street, we work through one or two access points and repair the pipe from the inside or replace it in place. There are two main methods: cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) lining and pipe bursting. Both fix the line underground, so what's above it stays untouched.

img.alt: Two J. Blanton plumbers setting up sewer camera and cable equipment beside a home's foundation before a trenchless sewer repair

blocks.h2: Why Trenchless Works Well in Elgin
blocks.intro: Elgin's older neighborhoods are where trenchless repair saves the most.

items.body: Narrow lots near downtown have big trees, old walks and garages over the sewer path. Lining keeps them in place.
When roots have opened most of the joints in a clay line, a liner seals all of them in one job.
Lines patched with different materials over the years can often be lined end to end, which gives you one continuous pipe.
Fewer and smaller openings mean less impact on the parkway, the sidewalk and your neighbors.

blocks.h2: Trenchless Sewer Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: Can an old clay line under a historic home be lined?
items.preview: Often, yes, if it's still holding its shape.
items.answer: Often, yes. If the camera shows the pipe is still round and open, a liner can go in and seal every joint. Badly broken or collapsed sections may need a spot repair first.

items.q: How long does a liner last?
items.preview: Decades. It's a seamless pipe inside the old one.
items.answer: Liners are designed to last for decades. Once cured, it's a seamless pipe with no joints for roots to enter.

items.q: How long does a trenchless repair take?
items.preview: Many are done in a day or two.
items.answer: Many residential jobs are done in a day or two, depending on length and how much prep the line needs.

items.q: Will lining reduce my pipe size?
items.preview: Slightly, but it usually flows as well or better.
items.answer: Slightly. The liner adds a thin wall, but its smooth surface with no joints or scale usually carries water as well as the old pipe or better.

items.q: How much does trenchless sewer repair cost in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on the line and method. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on how much of the line needs work, the depth, the method and access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
